ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List for USD transactions, and Luxembourg's national asset-freezing framework under the Law of 12 November 2004; mandatory PEP screening under FATF Recommendation 12 and EU AML/CFT directives; enhanced due diligence on PEPs, complex ownership, high-risk jurisdictions, and non-resident partners; ongoing transaction monitoring and risk-triggered EDD for the medium-risk orthopedic manufacturing segment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) e-filing portal: https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name must be in a Latin-script language (French, German, English, or Luxembourgish) with Latin transliteration recorded in the RCS; for an SCSp, the legal form descriptor 'SCSp' or 'société en commandite spéciale' must appear in the name; non-Roman script names must be accompanied by a certified transliteration and are subject to RCS acceptance.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg (in a way implying state sponsorship or official body)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name availability request is filed via LBR; if granted, the non-confusion certificate is valid for 90 days, with extension possible by filing a new request before expiry. If the RCS rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a written administrative objection with LBR within one month of rejection; after an upheld refusal, a judicial appeal may be brought before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within two months of notification; counsel should simultaneously submit a revised name to avoid blocking the incorporation timeline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is not permissible as the sole registered office for an SCSp engaged in physically licensed orthopedic implant manufacturing. The SCSp must maintain a physical registered office in Luxembourg where statutory records, management functions, and personnel are based. A domiciliation provider may furnish a physical Luxembourg address, but the production plant and quality assurance facility must be a separate, licensed physical site satisfying EU MDR 2017/745 and Pharma/Medical Device requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 70% probability of unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months, driven by EU MDR 2017/745 competent authority audits, Ministry of Health surveillance, and Luxembourg direct tax administration (ACD) substance verification for the manufacturing SCSp.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales); SCSp introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013 and governed by Articles 16-1 et seq., with subsidiary application of the general partnership provisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), under the supervision of the Ministry of Justice.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (direct taxes), and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Administration (VAT, registration duties); unified e-services portals: MyGuichet.lu, the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic RCS platform, and the eTVA electronic VAT filing platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The LU_SCSp is established by written partnership agreement (notarial deed not required unless real property is contributed) and registered electronically with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) via MyGuichet.lu by a Luxembourg-registered professional; registration automatically generates the 13-digit national identification number (matricule/NIF) issued by the LBR. The SCSp then files Formulaire 640 with the AEDT using LuxTrust/eIDAS credentials and is issued a Luxembourg VAT identification number in LU+8-digit format. Non-resident general partners must provide foreign tax identification certificates and may be required to appoint an AEDT-accepted tax representative; the SCSp must also register as an employer with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) when it hires personnel for the 3D-printing production facility.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: The SCSp lacks separate corporate tax personality; it is fiscally transparent for Luxembourg corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (MBT) and net wealth tax (NWT). All income, capital gains, deductions and tax credits are allocated to and taxed at partner level in proportion to partnership interests; a non-resident partner carrying on commercial activity through the SCSp is deemed to maintain a Luxembourg permanent establishment. For VAT purposes the SCSp is an independent taxable person: it must charge output VAT, may deduct input VAT, files periodic VAT returns, and its partners are jointly and severally liable for VAT debts of the partnership.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Luxembourg law permits an election under Article 175bis LIR to treat a transparent SCSp as a resident taxpayer subject to CIT, MBT and NWT, binding for at least five years. Hybrid mismatch rules under LIR Article 168quater (ATAD I/II) require partner-by-partner tax classification evidence, including foreign classification certificates (e.g., US Form W-8BEN-E, German Feststellungserklärung), before distributions are made. VAT elections available include waiver of the small-business franchise, VAT grouping (unité de TVA), OSS/Non-Union OSS registration for distance sales, and any statutory periodic option for the export or inward processing regime as applicable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA), implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC, administered by the AEDT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €35,000 annual taxable turnover for Luxembourg-established businesses under the VAT small-business franchise (franchise de taxe); this threshold does not apply to non-established suppliers, who must register from the first taxable euro. For distance sales of titanium orthopedic implants to non-taxable EU consumers, the EU-wide cross-border threshold of €10,000 applies and may be covered by OSS registration rather than local full registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No general real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime applies to B2B invoicing. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for public-sector contracts via the national PEPPOL (BIS Billing 3.0) network; B2B e-invoicing is permitted subject to authenticity-of-origin and integrity controls. VAT returns, EC Sales Lists and Intrastat/Extrastat supplementary declarations must be filed electronically through the eTVA portal using LuxTrust/eIDAS authentication, with API integration available for automated periodic filing; invoices must contain the EU statutory minimum data points and be archived in an authentic, legible format.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated (0%) treatment applies under Article 54 of the Luxembourg VAT Law to supplies of titanium orthopedic implants physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the supplier, the customer or a third party acting on their behalf, provided the exempt status of the customer is evidenced and the goods leave the EU within the legally required period. Ancillary services (international freight, insurance, loading and handling) may be zero-rated under Articles 55–56; intra-Community dispatches to EU hospitals or distributors holding a valid EU VAT number are zero-rated under Article 53, subject to inclusion in the EC Sales List. Input VAT embedded in export costs is refundable through the ordinary VAT refund mechanism, including the 8th Directive and 13th Directive procedures for non-established EU/non-EU businesses.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document) with IE599 exit-confirmation proof lodged via the EU Customs EDP (ELS/DELTA system) evidencing export office and actual EU departure
Transport document evidencing physical departure: Bill of Lading (sea), CMR waybill (road) or Air Waybill (air) with customs departure date
Commercial invoice (original set) stating Incoterms, export order reference, 0% VAT rate, and HS code for orthopedic implants; packing list with lot-level serial numbers for traceability

Payment and FX settlement evidence: SWIFT MT103, inward remittance certificate or letter-of-credit presentation demonstrating receipt of funds from the foreign buyer matching the contractual reference and invoice amount
Regulatory compliance file: EU MDR (2017/745) CE-marking certificate, quality-management and sterilization records, and trade-controls screening declaration for titanium powder precursors
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT verifies export zero-rating by cross-matching the IE599 customs exit record against the 180-day payment benchmark, transport and insurance documents, and partner-level capital-flow reconciliation. Any unexplained gap between shipment date and FX repatriation triggers VAT reassessment at 17% plus late-payment interest at 0.8% per commenced month and administrative fines. The ordinary limitation period is five years, extended to ten years in cases of fraud or false documentation. Criminal sanctions for fraudulent zero-rating claims include fines up to €250,000 and imprisonment from eight days to five years under Article 61 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, with proportional fines up to twice the tax evaded, joint and several liability of the SCSp general partner, and exclusion from the taxpayer good-faith compliance programme.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) operating within the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks; foreign-exchange policy competence is vested in the European Central Bank. Prudential and AML/CFT supervision of credit institutions, payment institutions and electronic money institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full current-account and capital-account convertibility under Articles 63 and 65 TFEU. No exchange-control authorization is required for foreign direct investment, partnership capital contributions, trade settlements, or profit distributions by an SCSp. The SCSp is fiscally transparent and distributions to non-resident partners are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax. Practical constraints are limited to the resident bank’s AML/CFT obligations under the law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02, EU and OFAC sanctions screening in USD clearing, Eurosystem balance-of-payments statistical reporting, and substance expectations for a pass-through manufacturing vehicle. Export proceeds can be retained indefinitely in EUR or foreign currency without any conversion mandate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The Grand Duchy imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio. Neither the BCL nor the CSSF requires repatriation, liquidation, or conversion of export receivables into euro. The only reporting layer is the resident credit institution’s obligation to transmit balance-of-payments and direct-investment statistics to the BCL under Regulation (EU) No 184/2005, as amended. The SCSp must supply the paying bank with the commercial invoice, transport documents, and the correct ISO purpose code for each inward receipt. Documentary retention of at least 10 years under Luxembourg commercial law is recommended, and physical cash movements in excess of EUR 10,000 crossing EU borders must be declared under Regulation (EU) 2018/1672.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: LOW-MEDIUM feasibility as a primary treasury rail. Luxembourg EMIs licensed under the law of 17 July 2020 implementing EMD2 and PSD2 may hold client funds, execute SEPA and SWIFT transfers, and issue e-money, but they are prohibited from extending credit, opening or confirming documentary credits under UCP 600, and they lack the global correspondent network required for USD trade settlements. An EMI can serve only as a support account for instant SEPA and corporate expense cards; the core cross-border exposure must remain with a full-service credit institution such as BCEE, BIL or Société Générale Luxembourg.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg AML law and CSSF Regulation 12-02 do not impose an absolute statutory physical-meeting requirement; remote onboarding is legally permissible using eIDAS qualified electronic signatures, certified video identification, and apostilled documentation provided the risk-based CDD file is complete. In practice, for an SCSp with a non-resident general partner classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced, tier-1 banks generally require at least one in-person identification of the authorized manager, a notarized or apostilled passport of the ultimate beneficial owner, and a video interview with the UBO. Recommended approach: one executive attends an in-person bank interview in Luxembourg, the UBO participates via secure video call, all corporate and identity documents are certified/apostilled, and a regulated Luxembourg law firm introduces the file to streamline authorization.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp registered as a partnership without legal personality creates uncertainty on contractual capacity and bank account signatory authority.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the partnership agreement (contrat de société), RCS registration extract of the SCSp, extract from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), power of attorney granted to the authorized signatory, and a Luxembourg legal opinion confirming that the general partner validly binds the SCSp and may open and operate bank accounts in its name.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intra-group non-EU capital injection exceeding EUR 250,000 prompts enhanced due diligence on source of funds and source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited IFRS or local GAAP financial statements of the contributing partner, SCSp capital account ledger, contributing partner board resolution, bank reference letter from the payer’s regulated institution, complete payment chain documentation, and the underlying direct-investment rationale with proof of Luxembourg substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through partnership perceived as a shell or brass-plate structure lacking economic substance in Luxembourg.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg substance pack evidencing administrative office or contracted service arrangements, local management decisions and bank instructions issued from the general partner’s Luxembourg address, payroll or outsourced employment records, audited accounts of the operating manufacturing affiliate, OECD-compliant transfer pricing documentation, and annual RCS filings confirming continuity of the registered office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment risk in the medical device distribution chain where the payer of invoices differs from the purchaser on the shipping documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full contractual chain comprising distribution agreements, end-user certificates, pro forma and final commercial invoices describing titanium orthopedic implants under ISIC 3250, CMR/B/L/AWB transport evidence, EU MDR or FDA conformity declarations, CE marking documentation, and reconciliation of each SWIFT payment to the corresponding transaction reference and invoice.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, adverse-media, or high-risk jurisdiction flags arising from a non-resident ultimate shareholder or limited partner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed CSSF and Wolfsberg-style beneficial ownership questionnaires, full identification of every natural person in the ownership chain with name, nationality and date of birth, jurisdictional risk rationale tied to EU and US hospital export markets, negative sanctions and media screening report from a reputable provider, and a board compliance attestation confirming no connection to designated persons or embargoed territories.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections must be effected by SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 pacs.008 from the limited partner’s credit institution to the SCSp’s Luxembourg operating account, using the ISO purpose code CAPC and a precise remittance reference to the partner’s capital account. USD-denominated injections clear through the correspondent banking network into the receiving bank’s USD omnibus account; EUR injections settle directly via Target2 or EBA CLEARING. The receiving bank captures transactions above EUR 100,000 for BCL external statistics, but no prior BCL authorization or foreign-exchange control form exists. Contributions in kind, such as titanium powder feedstock or electron-beam melting equipment, must be documented in a notarized contribution report, reflected in the RCS filing, and where appropriate declared for Luxembourg VAT purposes; source-of-funds evidence and beneficial ownership screens accompany all contributions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The treasury hierarchy for outbound trade disbursements is: (1) SWIFT gpi MT103 or pacs.008 with a unique end-to-end transaction reference for routine supplier payments below EUR 1,000,000; (2) commercial documentary credits under UCP 600 for high-value titanium feedstock and production consumables, issued via MT700, amended by MT707, and negotiated by the Luxembourg confirming bank with MT202 cover; (3) documentary collections under URC 522 for recurring lower-risk vendors; and (4) SEPA B2B Direct Debits for EEA-registered service providers. Every instruction must include the purchase order and invoice references, the Luxembourg VAT registration number, and the ISIC 3250 product descriptor. USD disbursements are executed through the bank’s cross-currency desk so that EUR/USD conversion is performed on the trade date with a single matched conversion, eliminating double-FX leakage and reducing settlement risk.

EUR/USD FX swap enabling spot-forward rollover for short-term liquidity bridging

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registered Office Confirmation (Déclaration Annuelle de Maintien du Siège)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due each calendar year within the month of the RCS registration anniversary; deposit required by month-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 10,000 per responsible officer under the amended Law of 19 December 2002; repeated non-filing flags the entity inactive and may lead to administrative strike-off and judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (Dépôt des Comptes Annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) / Central Balance Sheet Office (CDCLF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approve accounts within 6 months of FY-end and file within 1 month of approval; absolute cut-off 7 months after FY-end (31 July for a 31 December FYE).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under the Law of 19 December 2002: court-imposed fines of EUR 750 to EUR 25,000 per defaulting manager; the Commercial Court may order forced deposit; persistent non-compliance may trigger dissolution proceedings and adverse partner personal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Register Verification and Change Filing (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE section, Ministry of Finance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing once at registration; every transfer of partnership interests requires an RBE update within 30 days of the transaction; annual confirmation is made through the RCS annual declaration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines from EUR 250 to EUR 250,000; willful false declarations attract criminal sanctions (up to 5 years' imprisonment); the partnership may be barred from profit distributions while non-compliant.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Transparency Confirmation and Luxembourg Direct Tax Return (Déclaration Fiscale Annuelle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return for the transparent SCSp filed by 31 December of the year following the tax year; extended to 31 March in practice for calendar-year taxpayers, depending on professional filing agreements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of the amount of tax assessed at partner level and monthly interest of 0.6%; if the return is intentionally omitted, criminal fines apply and the tax authority may issue direct net-wealth assessments to corporate partners.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit by an approved réviseur d'entreprises becomes mandatory when the SCSp exceeds two of three criteria: balance-sheet total over EUR 6.0M, net turnover over EUR 12.05M, or average workforce over 50 employees; audit is also required if the partnership agreement imposes it, if the SCSp qualifies as a public-interest entity, or if it operates as a regulated AIF.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 implementing Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as issued by the EU is permitted for large partnerships and may be required for regulated investment vehicles; annual accounts are prepared in euros and filed electronically as XBRL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must keep a full RBE file identifying ultimate partners with at least 25% interest. Each transfer of limited-partner or general-partner interests must be filed within 30 days with a Luxembourg-certified validation. The yearly RCS registered-office declaration serves as the annual confirmation that beneficial-ownership data is complete and accurate; officers must distribute fresh UBO confirmations to partners before each distribution event.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (SCSp register of limited partners and general partners)
Register of Directors (general partner and manager appointments/resignation records)
Minute Book (partner and management committee resolutions)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City: 17% CIT + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax; commune rate varies)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent (no entity-level CIT, net wealth tax, or municipal business tax); IP Box: 80% exemption on qualifying IP income, effective rate approx. 4.99% for Luxembourg City; participation exemption: 100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains; notional interest deduction on equity increases; R&D investment tax credit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 522 (Déclaration spéciale des sociétés de personnes) filed via MyGuichet.lu eCDF portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end; extension available upon written request to the Luxembourg direct tax administration (AED).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification: SCSp name, RCS registration number, registered office, fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory identification; non-resident partners are disclosed but no Luxembourg tax is assessed on their allocated share absent a Luxembourg permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partners' schedule: full name, address, country of tax residence, and agreed profit-sharing percentages.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Each non-resident partner must be listed; tax residence certificates are not required at time of filing but must be available upon request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net income/(loss) per audited financial statements of the titanium orthopedic implant manufacturing activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Luxembourg-source income and income attributable to the Luxembourg permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: add-backs (fines, income taxes, excess borrowing costs, non-validated depreciation) and deductions (IP box, participation exemption, notional interest deduction).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjustments are computed at the SCSp level; the resulting tax base is allocated to partners in proportion to their legal profit share.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation key: taxable income/loss attributed to each general and limited partner for the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocation must mirror the SCSp partnership agreement; a non-resident partner's Luxembourg PE income remains taxable in Luxembourg by default assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Substance declaration: number of employees, premises, operational expenditures, and description of the electron beam metal 3D melting and implant finishing activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document physical substance to support treaty entitlements, advance pricing agreements, and transfer pricing positions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Default assessment by the AED; late-filing surcharge up to 10% of tax due; late-payment interest of 0.60% per month; administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 for willful non-filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 510 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed via MyGuichet.lu eCDF portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end; quarterly prepayments due 10 March, 10 June, 10 September, and 10 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification: matricule, RCS number, legal form, address of the Luxembourg permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Filing required for a non-resident corporate partner's Luxembourg PE; a Luxembourg tax representative must be appointed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net result from the implant manufacturing accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only PE-attributable profit; apply arm's-length allocation of intra-group sales of porous titanium implants.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs: non-deductible expenses (fines, income taxes, excessive representation costs, excess interest under ATAD interest limitation rules).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE must limit deductions to expenses actually attributable to the Luxembourg operation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: participation exemption on dividends and capital gains, IP box deduction (80% of net qualifying IP income), notional interest deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim IP box only for qualifying patents or software copyrights held and economically developed by the Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after utilization of loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE may offset only Luxembourg-source losses carried forward; municipal business tax component is limited to 10 years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation: 17% CIT, 7% solidarity surcharge, 6.75% municipal business tax (Luxembourg City); net wealth tax at 0.5% if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE is entitled to foreign tax credit in its residence state; remittance of PE profits to the head office is free of Luxembourg withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-payment interest of 0.60% per month; late-filing surcharge up to 10%; default assessment; administrative fine up to EUR 25,000 for fraudulent returns; publication of the assessment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory WHT on dividends distributed by Luxembourg companies (Art. 146 LIR); SCSp profit distributions are not dividends and are exempt from WHT due to fiscal transparency.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the beneficial owner must deliver a current Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) and a beneficial ownership declaration to the Luxembourg paying agent before payment; EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive applies at 0% for a qualifying 10% holding held for at least 12 months. For retrospective claims, file Form 24 with the Luxembourg direct tax administration within five years; the SCSp must maintain economic substance and DAC6 documentation to withstand the Principal Purpose Test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT: 0% on both interest and royalties under Luxembourg domestic law; treaties generally maintain 0% (some older treaties allow up to 10% on royalties); no Luxembourg source WHT is imposed, making the SCSp an efficient IP holding and financing vehicle.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 group consolidated turnover (non-SME threshold) triggers mandatory Master File and Local File preparation; EUR 750,000,000 group consolidated revenue triggers Country-by-Country Report filing with the Luxembourg AED.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg imposes no standalone ESR statute, but applies the substance-over-form doctrine, the abuse-of-law rule (Art. 6 AStG), ATAD anti-avoidance provisions (interest limitation, CFC, exit taxation), and DAC6 mandatory disclosure. The SCSp must maintain real premises, local decision-making, adequate employees, and proportionate operating expenditures to obtain tax residence certificates, sustain treaty benefits, and preserve advance pricing agreements and tax rulings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission or false declaration of the SCSp's Luxembourg PE income; fabricated invoices for titanium implant supplies; deliberate disregard of arm's-length pricing; misuse of pass-through status to conceal taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax up to 50% of evaded tax; late-payment interest at 0.60% per month; criminal fine up to EUR 25,000; imprisonment up to 5 years; publication of the judgment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing directors and the SCSp's general partner face personal civil restitution for the evaded tax, disqualification orders, asset freezes, travel bans under criminal procedure, and imprisonment; the corporate veil is pierced where the SCSp is used as a mere façade.
